I4_attribution_tie.STATUS: CAUSED AND FIXED. Merged as PR #1039.
I4_attribution_tie.v1_was_wrong: v1 said the engine emits a leechseed heal alongside the liquidooze damage, double-counting the mechanism, and that the +19 'coincidentally' equalled Leftovers. BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE. The engine already suppresses the drain under Liquid Ooze unconditionally -- gen3/generate_instructions.rs:3624-3647 is a hard if/else and no path emits both. And it was not a coincidence.
I4_attribution_tie.the_real_cause: a renderer predicate. events.rs drains_opponent keyed only on the opponent being seeded and both mons alive, so it planned a drain-heal slot the engine never emits. The reversed drain is a NEGATIVE Heal and emitted_heal counts only heal_amount > 0, so plan.heal ran one longer than emitted_heal, the reconcile marked the side unusable, and the seeder's Leftovers tick fell through to the [from] Leech Seed fallback. Ledger H.1.
I4_attribution_tie.the_identification: three-for-three, at three different max HPs: the mislabelled heal is always exactly the SEEDER'S OWN maxhp/16 -- Shiftry 312->19, Magmar 246->15, Meganium 275->17. It was not a coincidence that the value matched Leftovers. It WAS Leftovers.

I3_roll_inherited.STATUS: CAUSED for two rows. The third is a different shape and is reassigned.
I3_roll_inherited.the_cause: Pain Split averages the two mons' CURRENT HP, so its magnitude is a function of the HP left after the damage roll: a different legal roll gives a different Pain Split. movepainsplit is in the EXACT bucket (_ROLL_SCALED_SOURCES, engine_transition_differential.py:310-312, which does not contain 'residual' or 'movepainsplit'), so a 1 HP difference is compared for equality and rejected.
I3_roll_inherited.worked_19000016_2: Jirachi 266/266, Swalot 316 -> 276 after move=-40. floor((266+276)/2) = 271, so Swalot 276->271 = -5, and Jirachi's half is capped at 266 and silent. The engine arm at movepainsplit=-4 needs floor((266+s)/2) = s-4, i.e. s in {273,274}, i.e. a roll of 42 or 43 -- both legal. Verified independently by review.
I3_roll_inherited.scope_correction: v1 described 'Jirachi Ice Punches, Swalot Pain Splits' and 'the Pain Split differs by 1' for all three rows. That describes 19000016/2 only. 19000016/49 is Psychic, not Ice Punch.

disposition.detail: movepainsplit must be roll-aware -- either roll-scaled, or cascade-handled with a bound derived from the roll gap, as the capped-heal work does. The heal_to_full precedent at engine_transition_differential.py:301-310 is a genuine analogue. Requires a pin that fails when reverted.

I3_roll_inherited.19000198_22: RESTORED to I3 after review. An earlier v2 draft moved it to C93's crit-tag shape on the grounds that its MAJORITY arm is non-crit -- true and irrelevant, because the matcher accepts a boundary if ANY branch matches, so the row turns on the 6.25% crit arm. Both misses read 'attributed components differ', the EXACT-component path; a crit-tag rejection would surface as 'roll-scaled components differ'. So on p1 the crit arm CLEARED the roll check and the crit cross-check (engine_transition_differential.py:1342) and its direct hit agreed -- the symmetric difference contains only movepainsplit, -91 observed against -89, a 2 HP difference from a different legal crit roll. That is I3's mechanism unmixed, and the I3 fix closes it: 2/89 = 2.2%, inside the +/-9% band.
I3_roll_inherited.why_this_row_matters_most: it is the strongest argument for the I3 fix, not the weakest. It shows the exact-bucket rejection biting a MINORITY arm that has already passed the roll and crit gates -- so a roll-aware movepainsplit has to be branch-set-aware, not just tolerant on the majority arm. The other two rows both happen to differ by 1 and do not force that.
I3_roll_inherited.classifier_agrees: cert_sweep_readout.attribute_row puts 19000198/22 in I3_roll_inherited. The earlier draft's prose contradicted the binding instrument silently.

I5_boundary_truncation.v1_causal_claim_RETRACTED: v1 said 'a forced-replacement boundary is not a full turn: Showdown runs no residual phase'. That is FALSE as a general gen3 rule and the repo already said so. gen3 sends the replacement out BEFORE the residual block (generate_instructions.rs:3222-3246, PR #876, verified against the real sim by scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py::faintresiduals), so residuals run and APPLY TO THE REPLACEMENT. tests/fixtures/showdown/explosion-seed148.log.gz turn 7 is exactly this shape and shows Showdown healing the incoming replacement and emitting |upkeep.
I5_boundary_truncation.the_actual_distinguisher: whether the residual block ALREADY RAN, not the shape of the ply. An ACTION-phase faint defers residuals to the replacement ply, which then applies them to the replacements. A RESIDUAL-phase faint (both actives die inside the block) has already executed it, so the replacement ply is bare. Both remaining rows are the second kind. force_switch cannot distinguish them, and in this harness it is reconstructed from the self request only (src/pokezero/engine_world.py:411, :496), so it is true on side one for both.

disposition.downgraded_from: v1 said 'ENGINE or HARNESS FIX' and asserted 'the engine is answering for a turn that did not happen'. Neither is supported.
disposition.why_not_simply_a_fix: a correct fix needs a 'residuals already ran this turn' state marker that survives the world reconstruction, landed in the ENGINE's end_of_turn_triggered with the renderer replica following. A shape predicate cannot express it -- PR #1037 tried exactly that and was closed as a regression: it pushed 39 boundaries into skip:strict_all_branches_lossy, 37 of which previously MATCHED.
disposition.note: whether this is ultimately a fix or a comparison limit turns on that check, which has not been run.
disposition.the_limit_side: stated symmetrically so the label does not lean. At this boundary Showdown's protocol is BARE -- no |upkeep|, no components -- and per the_actual_distinguisher the discriminating fact (whether the residual block already ran) is a property of the PREVIOUS ply. Nothing observable at the boundary the differential is asked to evaluate separates the two cases, and engine_world.py:411/:496 reconstructs from the self request only. If the segmentation cannot be made to carry cross-step state, this is not settleable by this comparison -- which is exactly what the program reserves 'comparison limit' for. It stays UNDETERMINED because the harness DOES hold the prior step's protocol in the same game, so a look-back is possible.
